fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)

functional_requirements_axi_baseline_inh.text: All five AXI transaction channels + three ACE snoop channels use the same VALID/READY handshake. Source generates VALID; destination generates READY. Transfer occurs only when both VALID and READY are HIGH at a rising edge of ACLK.
Each ACE interface has a single clock signal ACLK, sampled on rising edge. All signal changes occur after the rising edge.
Reset signal ARESETn is active-LOW. Async assert; sync deassert.
On master and slave interfaces there must be no combinatorial paths between input and output signals (applies to AXI + ACE channels).
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary (inherited from AXI).

functional_requirements_ace_extensions.text: Every AR/AW transaction must drive ARDOMAIN[1:0] / AWDOMAIN[1:0] selecting one of: Non-shareable, Inner Shareable, Outer Shareable, System.
A Non-shareable domain contains a single master. Inner / Outer Shareable domains include additional masters. System domain includes all masters in the system.
A memory location indicated as being in the System domain cannot be held in any cache.
Coherent transactions on AR/AW use ARSNOOP[3:0] / AWSNOOP[2:0] to encode the coherent operation. Permitted encodings depend on ARBAR[0] + ARDOMAIN combinations (Tables C3-7, C3-8).

ReadShared requests a copy that may be shared. ReadClean requests a clean copy. ReadNotSharedDirty forbids SharedDirty response. ReadUnique requests an exclusive copy (invalidates other caches). CleanUnique cleans local + invalidates others (no data transfer). MakeUnique invalidates other caches without data transfer (used before full-line overwrites).

Cache-maintenance transactions: CleanShared writes back dirty + retains a Shared copy. CleanInvalid writes back dirty + invalidates. MakeInvalid invalidates without writing back (used when content is discarded).

Memory-update writes: WriteBack writes a dirty line and invalidates it. WriteClean writes a dirty line and retains a Clean copy. Evict notifies the interconnect that a line has been removed (no data). WriteEvict (optional, with AWUNIQUE) writes back UniqueClean lines for snoop-filter tracking.

Coherent writes for non-cached masters (ACE-Lite or full ACE): WriteUnique writes a partial line through coherency (other caches invalidated first). WriteLineUnique writes a full line through coherency.
AxBAR[0]=1 indicates a barrier transaction. ARSNOOP=0b0000 and AWSNOOP=0b000 are used for barriers. AxBAR[1] encodes barrier type: Memory_Barrier vs Synchronization_Barrier.
Barrier transactions can have any shareability domain; the choice of domain determines the barrier scope (Non-shareable / Inner / Outer / System).

Distributed Virtual Memory (DVM) messages use ARSNOOP encodings DVMComplete (0b1110) and DVMMessage (0b1111). DVM is used for TLB invalidate, branch predictor invalidate, instruction cache invalidate, and virtual address synchronization across coherent masters.

Read response is extended to RRESP[3:0]: [1:0] original OKAY/EXOKAY/SLVERR/DECERR; [2] PassDirty (cache line dirty wrt memory — receiver responsible for write-back); [3] IsShared (another cache may hold a copy).
RRESP[3:2] must be constant for all data transfers within a burst.
RRESP[3:2] must be LOW for ReadNoSnoop, Barrier, and DVM transactions.
Write response is extended to BRESP[2]: DataTransfer indicator, used for WriteBack/WriteClean pass-dirty scenarios.
Snoop address channel AC: interconnect drives ACADDR, ACSNOOP[3:0], ACPROT[2:0], ACVALID; cached master drives ACREADY.
Snoop response channel CR: cached master drives CRRESP[4:0], CRVALID; interconnect drives CRREADY. CRRESP bits: [0] DataTransfer, [1] Error, [2] PassDirty, [3] IsShared, [4] WasUnique.
Snoop data channel CD: cached master drives CDDATA, CDLAST, CDVALID; interconnect drives CDREADY. The CD bus may be narrower than RDATA/WDATA.

Snoop channel dependency: master must wait for both ACVALID and ACREADY before asserting CRVALID. Master must also wait for both ACVALID and ACREADY before asserting CDVALID. CRVALID and CDVALID must not depend on CRREADY/CDREADY.

RACK signal is asserted by the master for one ACLK cycle on the rising edge following RLAST=HIGH+RVALID+RREADY, confirming the master has accepted the read response. WACK is asserted by the master one cycle after BVALID+BREADY, confirming the write response. RACK/WACK enable the interconnect to know that ordering hazards have been resolved before issuing dependent snoops.
Cache line uses a 5-state model: UniqueClean (UC), UniqueDirty (UD), SharedClean (SC), SharedDirty (SD), Invalid (I). UD/SD lines are responsible for eventual write-back. UC/SC match main memory.
On a snoop that requires invalidation (ReadUnique, CleanInvalid, MakeInvalid), the snooped cache must transition the line to Invalid and the CRRESP IsShared bit must be LOW.

If the cache line moves from a Dirty state to Clean as a result of a snoop, CRRESP[2] PassDirty must be asserted. If the line moves from Dirty to Invalid (except via MakeInvalid), PassDirty must be asserted. For MakeInvalid, PassDirty can be 0 or 1.
PassDirty=1 with DataTransfer=0 is illegal — if responsibility is passed, data must be transferred. IsShared=1 is illegal for ReadUnique / CleanInvalid / MakeInvalid.

ACE-Lite is a subset for non-cached masters. They do not implement the AC/CR/CD snoop channels (no local cache to snoop). They may issue coherent reads (ReadOnce / ReadNoSnoop) and coherent writes (WriteUnique / WriteLineUnique / WriteNoSnoop). RRESP[3:2] are observed but the master never returns IsShared/PassDirty.

error_response_conditions: Inherited AXI: FIFO/buffer overrun, unsupported transfer size, write to read-only location, slave timeout, access to disabled function.
ACE-specific: CRRESP[1] Error — snoop response indicates a failure in the cached master.
Illegal AxDOMAIN/AxSNOOP/AxBAR combinations (must be detected and treated as a protocol violation; the interconnect may return DECERR or SLVERR).

protocol_overview.snoop_protocol: Address-based on AC channel; response on CR; optional data on CD

evidence.quote: The ACE protocol provides hardware cache coherency support and is an extension of the AXI4 protocol.
A shareability domain is a set of masters. The ACE protocol specifies four levels of shareability domain: Non-shareable, Inner Shareable, Outer Shareable, System.
AxDOMAIN[1:0]: 0b00 Non-shareable, 0b01 Inner Shareable, 0b10 Outer Shareable, 0b11 System.

Coherent ARSNOOP encodings: 0b0000 ReadOnce, 0b0001 ReadShared, 0b0010 ReadClean, 0b0011 ReadNotSharedDirty, 0b0111 ReadUnique, 0b1011 CleanUnique, 0b1100 MakeUnique. Cache maintenance: 0b1000 CleanShared, 0b1001 CleanInvalid, 0b1101 MakeInvalid. DVM: 0b1110 DVM Complete, 0b1111 DVM Message.

Coherent AWSNOOP encodings: 0b000 WriteNoSnoop (Non-shareable) / WriteUnique (Shareable), 0b001 WriteLineUnique, 0b010 WriteClean, 0b011 WriteBack, 0b100 Evict, 0b101 WriteEvict, 0b000 Barrier (with AWBAR[0]=1).
RRESP[2] PassDirty bit; RRESP[3] IsShared bit. The IsShared and PassDirty responses must be constant for all data transfers within a burst.

evidence.quote: CRRESP[4:0]: [0] DataTransfer, [1] Error, [2] PassDirty, [3] IsShared, [4] WasUnique.

evidence.quote: The master must wait for both ACVALID and ACREADY to be asserted before asserting CRVALID. The master must wait for both ACVALID and ACREADY to be asserted before asserting CDVALID.

evidence.spec_section: C5.2 General requirements for snoop transactions / Table C5-4
evidence.quote: Cache line state abbreviations: UC UniqueClean. UD UniqueDirty. SC SharedClean. SD SharedDirty. I Invalid.

If the cache line moves from a Dirty state to a Clean state, the PassDirty snoop response bit must be asserted. If the line moves from a Dirty state to the Invalid state, as a result of any snoop transaction except MakeInvalid, the PassDirty snoop response bit must be asserted.
